requirements.requirement: Run a nightly backup of /srv/inventory/data from node2 to node1.
requirements.summary: An enabled, active systemd timer schedules the backup daily at 02:00. Multiple executions completed successfully, including after both nodes were restarted, and the resulting archive on node1 was updated.

requirements.requirement: Store dated archives under /var/backups/inventory on node1.
requirements.summary: A nonempty, date-named archive existed at /var/backups/inventory/inventory-2026-10-01.tar.gz, passed gzip/tar inspection, contained the source data/ directory, and persisted across node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain only the last seven days of archives.
requirements.summary: The receiver implements age-based pruning, and a synthetic archive made eight days old was directly shown to be deleted by the next successful backup while the current archive remained intact.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The nightly timer is enabled, end-to-end node2-to-node1 backups succeed, dated archives are stored at the required destination, and the seven-day retention policy was behaviorally tested. The provider-wide restart protocol is strong for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, recovered system/service state, preserved data, and a successful post-restart backup.
limitations: The source path did not exist initially and was created empty, so archive inspection demonstrates correct handling of the current empty directory but does not exercise fidelity for actual inventory files.
The scheduled 02:00 timer firing was not observed naturally; scheduling was established from the enabled timer configuration and successful manual executions of the same service.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the previously absent source directory and transfer credentials was a necessary prerequisite (cmd-43f5fa9ce59a460a); the receiver account, archive directory, forced-command endpoint, SSH host keys, and runtime directory supported the required transfer (cmd-60104e9acaca4192, cmd-3dc2fdf4be82461d, cmd-ea544101366f4dd8); and the systemd units implemented the requested schedule (cmd-6651b01e9b704f7b). The synthetic old archive was a bounded retention probe and was fully removed by the tested backup (cmd-658db625b0134062, cmd-8e4c331f78244e23). Restart commands were required provider evidence. Final snapshots show no failed services or package damage, and port 22 was already exposed before execution.
